title: [Feedback] idea: Pray together — walk through the people on your heart one at a time, not as a list
body: ### The idea "On our hearts" is a list. The design reference adds a way to **pray through it** — one person at a time, full-screen, so you can actually pray instead of scroll. The `pray_together` button on My Day today just navigates to `/prayer`; this makes that promise real. Design reference: **`Prayer Session - preview.html`** in the design kit (the one-at-a-time session flow, keyboard + thumb). ### What it should do - A **"Pray together"** launch on the On-our-hearts page (a quiet card above the held list: *"Pray through them one at a time"*), shown only when there's someone with an open prayer. - Tapping it opens a **full-screen session** — one card per person, in the page's held order: - their name, avatar, tags; - the open prayers for that person (the burden + "asked N days ago"); - **"I prayed for {first}"** marks it and advances (device-local, per day — the app has no shared "who prayed" in Firestore). - Progress bar ("N of M"), **Back / Skip**, keyboard (`space`/`enter` = prayed & next, `←`/`→` move, `esc` leave). - An **end-of-session recap**: "You prayed for N of M" with the people you carried, then **Go through again** / **Close**. ### Scope - Desktop On-our-hearts page only, matching the design reference (the mobile prayer page already has its own carry flow). - Device-local per-day marking, consistent with the mobile "I prayed just now" pattern — no new Firestore field, no shared "who prayed" (deliberate, per the repo's existing decision). ### Not this No statuses, no testimonies, no editing, no shared team recap, no metrics, no reminders. _Reported from the design review of the `Prayer Session - preview.html` artifact._

title: A trainee is not paired to one full-timer — every full-timer stands over every trainee (drop the "your full-timer" model)
body: ### The design decision (answered 24 Aug 2026, in the design reference) > **A full-timer is not caring for particular trainees. Every full-timer stands over every trainee.** The one-to-one pairing is **gone** — no `FT_OF[me]`, no "your full-timer", no per-trainee assignment anywhere in the UI. A trainee's work is seen and answered by the **whole team** of full-timers. Why it outranks everything else: the current open feedback (#544 the on-campus goal, #545 questions that aren't about a person) both read from this layer. Until the pairing is removed, those features silently inherit "one carer" semantics the team has already abandoned. ### What that means here (production) - `src/lib/walking.ts` still holds `FT_TRAINEES` / `FT_OF`, and `fullTimerOf(uid)` gates the trainee's view of who writes to them. - `src/lib/attention.ts:152` — a trainee's attention feed only surfaces messages from `fullTimerOf(uid)`. - `src/lib/inbox.ts:120` — `traineeWaitingItems` filters `m.from !== ft`; unpaired trainees get an empty cockpit. - `src/views/landings/LandingTrainee.tsx:229-232` — "What's waiting on you — your full-timer's nudges/questions" reads `fullTimerOf(uid)`. - `src/lib/firstRun.ts:140` — first-run asks "Ask your full-timer something real". - `src/components/modals/NewContactModal.tsx:172` and `LogInteractionModal.tsx:177` — the "who connected" default resolves through `fullTimerOf`. - `src/views/Settings.tsx:1676-1698` — the "Walking together" block still pairs each trainee with one full-timer. ### The correction, per the design reference 1. **The pairing stops meaning a relationship.** Keep one predicate — *is this person a full-timer* — and one set: *the trainees*. `FT_TRAINEES[uid]` currently doubles as "am I an ft" in several gates; those should read a plain `isFullTimer(uid)` instead, so removing the pairing doesn't quietly switch features off. 2. **A message is from a person, so it says that person's name.** "the full-timer who cares for you" → **"Mei wrote to you"**. A trainee's queue and "What's waiting on you" should accept a note from **any** full-timer and name the writer. Where no one person is meant, say **"the team"** — never "your full-timer". 3. **The oversight inbox widens to every full-timer.** `inboxItemsFor` already surfaces the whole team's activity; that becomes the rule everywhere, not an exception in one feed. 4. **Settings → "Who's caring for whom" / the "Walking together" pairing UI is superseded** — the app no longer holds a pairing, so the manager should be removed or archived, not kept as a live control that re-creates the model. 5. **Gospel partners are untouched** — trainee↔trainee pairing for a term is a different thing. The design reference has this fully built (see its "NO PAIRING" section, cache-bust `?v=ft1`): `isFullTimer(uid)` / `isTrainee(uid)` / `fullTimerIds()` / `traineeIds()` read the STAFF roster, every gate is switched off the pairing, and a word is named after its writer. This issue asks to port that correction.

title: Phase 5: Translation Batch Prefetching, Mobile App Parity & Offline Caching
body: Follow-up to #351 (Phase 5): ### Summary Add intelligent viewport/list prefetching, offline translation fallback, and mobile app parity (`apps/mobile`). ### Scope - **Batch Prefetching:** - Prefetch visible list items upon feed load (e.g. 20 prayers at once in a single `/api/translate` call). - Background warming of cache for frequently viewed contacts and pinned notes. - **Mobile Parity (`apps/mobile`):** - Integrate translation service in React Native mobile views (Today, Prayers, Messages, People). - Use AsyncStorage for mobile L2 cache. - **Offline & Fallback Polish:** - Graceful fallback to original text on network failure or rate limits with retry indicators. ### Acceptance Criteria - Lists load with minimal perceived translation delay via batch prefetching. - Mobile client supports full Spanish mode with cached translations.

title: Phase 4: Dynamic UGC Translation Integration across Prayers, People, Messages & Notes
body: Follow-up to #351 (Phase 4): ### Summary Wire the translation hook and `<Translate />` component into dynamic User-Generated Content (UGC) across the application. ### Scope - **Prayers & Testimonies:** - `PrayerList.tsx`, `AnsweredList.tsx`, and mobile `PrayerListMobile.tsx`. - Translate prayer burdens, prayer titles, update notes, and answered testimonies. - **People & Directory:** - `ContactDetailsModal.tsx`, `Directory.tsx`, and `History.tsx`. - Translate contact notes, interaction log summaries, and next step reminders. - **Messages & Chat:** - `Messages.tsx`, `chat.ts`, and mobile chat threads. - Live translation of incoming chat messages with reactive subscription. - **Coordination Notes & The Board:** - `CoordinationNotes.tsx`, `EmbedCoordinationDoc.tsx`. - Markdown-aware translation preserving headings, checklists, links, and code blocks. - **Original Content Switcher:** - Add an inline 'Ver original' / 'Show original' toggle for translated user cards. ### Acceptance Criteria - User-entered text in any section translates seamlessly when Spanish is active. - Clicking 'Ver original' toggles back to the raw source text. - Comprehensive unit tests across components.

title: Phase 3: Static UI Strings Localization (i18n) for Shell, Modals & Navigation
body: Follow-up to #351 (Phase 3): ### Summary Extract and localize all static UI strings (navigation tabs, buttons, modal headers, empty states, system alerts, and notifications) into an English/Spanish dictionary. ### Scope - **UI Localization Dictionary (`src/locales/es.json` / `src/locales/en.json`):** - Navigation items: Coordination Notes, People, The Journey, On our hearts, History, Settings, More menu. - Action buttons: 'Add someone', 'Log a visit', 'Smart Import', 'Quick Add', 'Export CSV', 'Save', 'Cancel'. - Modal titles, empty state descriptions, error messages, and form labels. - **Integration:** - Lightweight dictionary helper `t(key, fallback)` integrated with layout and language preference context. - Zero-latency, deterministic rendering for all chrome and static controls. ### Acceptance Criteria - When Spanish is toggled on, all shell controls and UI buttons switch instantly to Spanish. - Unit tests verify all dictionary keys exist and render correctly.

title: Phase 2: Client Translation Engine, Multi-Tier Caching & Language Preference Toggle
body: Follow-up to #351 (Phase 2): ### Summary Implement the client-side translation engine, reactive hooks, multi-tier caching (L1 React state / memory + L2 IndexedDB / localStorage), and user language preference toggle. ### Scope - **Translation Client Core (`src/lib/translator.ts`):** - Content hashing (SHA-256 / Murmur3) matching backend. - L1 (in-memory LRU) + L2 (IndexedDB / localStorage) client cache. - Request batcher & debouncer (50ms queue) calling `POST /api/translate`. - **React Hooks & Primitives:** - `useTranslate(text, options)` hook. - `<Translate text={...} />` component with loading skeleton and error fallback. - **Language Preference & UI Controls:** - Add `language?: 'en' | 'es'` to `userPreferences` schema and Firestore subscription. - Language toggle selector in `TopNav.tsx`, `MobileNav.tsx`, and `Settings.tsx`. ### Acceptance Criteria - Seamless synchronous lookup for already-cached translations with zero layout shift. - Language toggle flips app preference and reactivity triggers live re-rendering. - Full unit test coverage.

title: [Macro study] Expand the command palette + central shortcut registry
body: Part of #325 · **Code** ## Problem Keyboard handling is ad hoc and undiscoverable: `⌘K` in `GlobalSearch.tsx:295`, `⌘Enter` in `Thread.tsx`, `TodoComposer.tsx`, `LogVisitModal.tsx`, and `FeedbackFAB.tsx` — five separate listeners, no registry, nothing listed anywhere. The ⌘K palette offers four quick actions with no way to learn what else exists. ## What Macro does `apps/web/src/lib/core/hotkey/` — a registry where every command declares its scope, description, condition, and handler, so the same registration both binds the key and populates the command palette. Shortcuts teach themselves. ## Explicitly NOT adopting Their leader grammar (`c`+letter creates, `g`+letter goes) and vim navigation (`j`/`k`, `gg`, `shift+G`). Macro serves ~15 engineers living in the tool 8 hours a day; this app serves students and Full-timers opening it a few times a week, often on a phone. Also skipping their priority chain and scope inheritance — far more machinery than this needs. ## Scope - A small registry: id, scope, description, handler - Both binds the shortcut and populates the ⌘K palette - Migrate the five existing ad-hoc listeners onto it - Palette lists available actions with their shortcuts ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Every existing shortcut still works - [ ] The palette lists actions the user can currently take, filtered by role - [ ] Registering a command in one place makes it both bound and discoverable

title: [Macro study] Four new to-do creation entry points
body: Part of #325 · **Code + light design** ## Problem To-dos can be created from two places: highlighting a line on a Board page, and from an interaction. Macro's argument is that trackers go stale because logging costs a context switch — they made tasks creatable from seven places for exactly this reason. ## Scope — four new entry points 1. **From an attendance absence** — marking someone absent on the Gatherings screen is the exact moment someone thinks "I should check on them." Highest value of the four. 2. **From the visit log form** — `Visit.followUpTaskId` already exists in the data model, so this is wiring, not schema. Makes creating the follow-up part of writing the visit up rather than a separate step. 3. **From a chat message** — hover / long-press → "Make a to-do", carrying the message as source. Mirrors the Board highlight flow already built. 4. **From a prayer** — turn a burden into a concrete follow-up while keeping the prayer linked as source. ## Implementation note One shared helper over `addTodo` in `src/lib/todos.ts`; each site differs only in which source it links. The existing `sourceDocId` / `sourceInteractionId` pattern extends naturally. ## Design needed Small — the affordance in four placements. Reuse the existing "Make a to-do" treatment from the Board. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] All four create a to-do linked back to its source - [ ] The source is visible on the resulting to-do row - [ ] Available on mobile where the source screen exists

title: [Macro study] Role-aware first-run checklist
body: Part of #325 · **Design + code** ## Problem There is no first-run experience. New trainees arrive every semester, and the four roles (Full-timer / Trainee / Student / Community) see substantially different apps. ## What Macro does `apps/web/src/features/getting-started/getting-started-types.ts` — a checklist where each row has an optional `isComplete()` read reactively from **live state**, plus `observe()` for event-driven completion, defaulting to "clicking it completes it". Their comment on why completion is derived rather than remembered: > never persisted itself, so it stays honest when e.g. a tool is disconnected ## Scope - Dismissible checklist on Home, rows differing per role - Completion derived from real state — "logged your first conversation" is true because they did, not because they clicked a button once - Collapsible sections, persisted per user ## Design needed Checklist layout, per-role row sets, and copy for four roles in the app's existing voice. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Each role sees rows relevant to what they can actually do - [ ] Completion reads live state; deleting the underlying data un-completes the row - [ ] Dismissible, and stays dismissed

title: [Macro study] Live contact pill with hover preview
body: Part of #325 · **Design + code** ## Problem Attaching a contact to a message stores `ChatAttachment { type, id, name, subtitle }` — a display cache written at attach time. It goes stale, and checking one fact about the person means opening `ContactDetailsModal.tsx` (2,402 lines). ## What Macro does Every @mention renders as a live pill carrying its target's *current* metadata — a task pill shows the task's status and priority — and previews on hover. Context without a click, and the pill can't go stale because it reads live. ## Scope - Contact pill showing stage and last-seen, read live rather than from the cached `subtitle` - Hover preview card on desktop; tap-to-preview on mobile - Contacts only for now; the other seven `ChatAttachment` types can follow if this lands well ## Design needed Pill treatment (including stage colour, which already exists as `StageChip`) and the preview card. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Pill reflects a stage change without the message being re-sent - [ ] Preview shows enough to answer "who is this and where are they at" without opening the modal - [ ] Works on mobile web and in `apps/mobile/`

title: [Macro study] One conversation thread per person; retire the admin Comments tab
body: Part of #325 · **Design + code** · ⚠️ **Has a privacy consequence — read before designing** ## Problem A conversation about one person can live in three places today: 1. `contacts/{id}/threads` — the walking-together thread (Trainee-visible) 2. The Comments tab in `ContactDetailsModal.tsx` (~line 2079) — gated `role === "admin" || isAdmin`, **Full-timers only** 3. Messages, with the contact attached via `ChatAttachment` Someone asking "what did we say about Sarah?" has to check all three. ## What Macro does *"Every deal gets its own channel, automatically, pinned right to the deal record."* Their argument: a CRM comment box always loses to where the conversation really happens, because people comment *and then* go ping the channel anyway. So the record's notes ARE the chat system, not a parallel one. ## ⚠️ Blocker — decide before this is designed The Comments tab is Full-timer-only; the walking-together thread is Trainee-visible. **Merging them changes who can read pastoral oversight notes that were written under a different expectation.** This is a privacy change, not just a data migration. Pick one: - **(recommended)** Migrated comments carry a visibility flag and the merged thread filters by role — preserves the original audience while still giving one place to look. Costs a `firestore.rules` change. - Comments migrate into a Full-timer-only section of the merged thread. - Existing comments stay in place; only *new* conversation goes to the thread. ## Scope - `contacts/{id}/threads` becomes the single conversation surface - Comments migrated per the decision above, with a migration script - Attaching a contact in Messages links into that same thread rather than starting a parallel one - `firestore.rules` updated and reproduced against the emulator **before** the rule is edited (rules deploys have their own CI gate — budget for it) ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Visibility decision recorded in this issue before design starts - [ ] No existing comment becomes readable by someone who could not read it before - [ ] Emulator-backed rules tests, red before green - [ ] Migration is reversible or dry-runnable

title: [Macro study] Shared action vocabulary + shared row menu
body: Part of #325 · **Design + code** ## Problem Row actions differ per view — the same intent is worded and placed differently on a person, a prayer, a visit, and a gathering. Users learn the app per screen instead of once. ## What Macro does Defines an action vocabulary once and applies it to every object type — `apps/web/src/lib/core/hotkey/tokens.ts` has `entity.action.{markDone, markRead, delete, rename, share, favorite, createReminder, assignee, status, ...}`. Same key, same menu, same wording regardless of what the object is. Their keyboard reference has a single "Entity Actions" section covering all types. ## Scope - Agree one action set — done, follow up later, share, make a to-do, open — and the exact wording, in the app's existing warm voice - One row/overflow menu component consumed by person, prayer, visit, and gathering rows - First consumer is the merged attention feed (#330), so co-design with it ## Design needed The overflow menu, its trigger, and mobile (long-press drawer) treatment. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] One menu component used by all four row types - [ ] "Done" means the same thing everywhere - [ ] Wording reviewed against the existing nav voice ("The Journey", "On our hearts", "Looking back")

title: [Macro study] Notification stacking by target
body: Part of #325 · **Design + code** · Pairs with #330 ## Problem `NotificationCenter.tsx` renders notifications flat. Three people commenting on one contact produces three rows, so the one thing that actually needed attention gets buried. This matters more here than in a workspace tool — notification volume per person is low, so a flat list is mostly noise around a few signals. ## What Macro does Collapses all notifications about the same entity into a single row showing the most recent, with the rest behind a collapsible list (`DEFAULT_VISIBLE_COUNT = 3`), and lets you mark the whole stack read or done at once. See `apps/web/src/features/entity/extractors-notification/notification-stacks.tsx`. ## Scope Group rows by target entity, show a count ("3 new on Sarah"), expand on demand, mark-all-done on the stack. ## Design needed Stacked row treatment, count badge, expanded state. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Multiple notifications about one contact render as one row with a count - [ ] Expanding shows the individual entries - [ ] Mark-done on the stack clears all of them

title: [Macro study] Merge attention surfaces into one feed with a done action
body: Part of #325 · **Design + code** · Blocked on #326 (read/done model) and #327 (date bucketing) ## Problem "What needs my attention" is split across three surfaces: - My Day's hand-assembled sections (`src/views/MyDay.tsx`, 1,192 lines) - `FromTraineesInbox` — the Full-timer oversight feed - `NotificationCenter` — the bell, a separate list entirely Someone has to check all three to know where they stand. And `src/lib/inboxReads.ts` only tracks *scanned*, which is passive — without a "done", the list only grows, so it stops being a list anyone can finish, and people stop opening it. ## What Macro does One list holding email, messages, @mentions, task assignments, and agent results. `e` marks done and removes the item. Their framing: *"You can think of the Signal view as your action list."* The stance is that you should check exactly one thing. **Not adopting:** their AI-sorted Signal/Noise split (volume doesn't justify it, and the failure mode — AI hides something pastoral — is worse than the problem), and Inbox-Zero-as-pressure. A list of people you haven't followed up with is not disposable the way email is; "clearing" a person is a strange verb, and a UI that rewards emptying the list can teach people to dismiss rather than follow up. Take *"done is distinct from seen"*; leave the pressure to reach zero. ## Scope - One attention feed on My Day carrying team activity, to-do assignments, thread questions, and notifications - Explicit per-row "done" that removes it, built on #326 - Date-group headers from #327 - Bell becomes push delivery only, not a second list ## Design needed Row anatomy per item kind, the done affordance, group headers, empty state. Desktop, `MyDayMobile.tsx`, and `apps/mobile/`. ## Watch The feed reads contacts, interactions, a `collectionGroup` over threads, notifications, and to-dos. My Day already does several of these — measure read volume before adding more, and check whether new composite indexes are needed. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] One feed replaces the three surfaces; the bell no longer maintains a parallel list - [ ] Marking done removes the row and persists per-user - [ ] Each of the four roles sees an appropriate feed - [ ] Firestore read count per load measured and recorded

title: [Macro study] Audit and derive Contact activity fields
body: Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** ## Problem `Contact` carries `lastSeen`, `lastContactedDate`, `lastContactedBy`, `lastContactedById`, and `hasNewActivity`. All of these look derivable from interactions, visits, and attendance — but if any is hand-entered, or written at only some of the call sites, it goes stale silently. A stale `lastContactedDate` breaks exactly the question the app exists to answer: who have we not seen in a while. ## What Macro does From their CRM docs: *"records create themselves … stages are all manual: Macro doesn't yet know where a company lies in your pipeline and relies on you."* A clean line between what the system can observe and what only a person knows. Their "Last Interaction" is a sortable column precisely because it is never typed. Stage stays manual here too — that is judgment, and correctly a human's. ## Scope 1. Map every write of the five fields across web (`src/lib/`, `src/views/`, `src/components/modals/`) and `apps/mobile/` 2. Route them through one derived update triggered by logging an interaction, a visit, or an attendance mark 3. Remove any path that accepts them as direct user input ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Logging an interaction, a visit, and an attendance mark each update the fields identically - [ ] No UI writes these fields directly - [ ] Tests cover all three event types - [ ] Audit findings recorded in the issue before the fix lands, so the size of the drift is known

title: [Macro study] Frecency ranking in Global Search
body: Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · Highest value-per-line item in the study ## Problem `src/components/layout/GlobalSearch.tsx` does substring filtering, caps each group at `GS_MAX = 4`, and applies **no ranking**. With no query, "recent people" sorts by `updatedAt` — which is *someone else's* edit, not your usage. So the people you open every day are not the people you are shown. ## What Macro does `crates/frecency` computes, per user per entity: ``` frequency = log2(event_count + 2) recency = Σ over last 10 events of exp(-0.1 × hours_ago) × weight score = 0.7 × frequency + 0.3 × recency weights: open = +2.0, ping = 0.0, close = -1.0 ``` The negative close weight is the interesting part: opening something and immediately closing it is evidence it was the *wrong* result, so it demotes itself. Their own client ships a much cheaper version for the command palette — `apps/web/src/features/command/recency.ts` is ~20 lines, a persisted `Record<commandId, timestamp>`. **That is the version to copy**, not the Rust service. ## Scope - Track opens in a per-uid localStorage store, reusing the pub/sub pattern already in `src/lib/inboxReads.ts` - Rank results by score; keep the substring filter as the gate (frecency only orders what already matched) - Consider whether `GS_MAX = 4` should rise once ordering is meaningful ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Opening a contact repeatedly floats it to the top of the no-query list - [ ] Open-then-immediately-close does not promote a result - [ ] Scoring is a pure function with unit tests; storage is tested separately

title: [Macro study] Shared date bucketing util (Today / Yesterday / This Week / Older)
body: Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · Feeds the merged attention feed's grouping ## Problem Date grouping is implemented inline in History, My Day, and the activity feed, each slightly differently. The merged attention feed will want the same grouping, which would make a fourth copy. ## What Macro does `crates/models_grouping/src/date_buckets.rs` — a fixed vocabulary as three tiny pure functions: | Bucket | Range | Order | |---|---|---| | Today | 0 days | 0 | | Yesterday | 1 day | 1 | | This Week | 2–6 days | 2 | | Last Week | 7–13 days | 3 | | This Month | 14–30 days | 4 | | Last Month | 31–60 days | 5 | | Older | 61+ days | 6 | Their docs frame it as a product feature, not formatting: it "keeps a busy list scannable without changing any of your filters or sorting." ## Scope `bucketFor(date)`, `bucketLabel(key)`, `bucketOrder(key)` in a shared util, built on the existing `daysSince` / `parseMs` in `src/components/landing/helpers.ts`. Adopt in History, My Day, and the activity feed. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Three pure functions, no view imports - [ ] Unit tests at every boundary: 0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 13, 14, 30, 31, 60, 61 days - [ ] Existing groupings in History / My Day / activity render identically or better - [ ] Warm labels agreed — the app says "Looking back", not "This Month", so copy should match the app's voice rather than Macro's

title: [Macro study] Unify read/done state into one per-user model
body: Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · **Prerequisite for the merged attention feed** ## Problem Five mechanisms currently answer fragments of one question — "has this person seen / dealt with this?": - `src/lib/inboxReads.ts` — localStorage, per-uid, ids like `contact:<id>` (already an entity ref) - `src/lib/convHides.ts` — localStorage, hidden conversations - `src/lib/messageHides.ts` — localStorage, hidden messages - `Notification.readBy` / `dismissedBy` — Firestore arrays - `Contact.reviewed` — a boolean on the shared domain object Three storage strategies, no shared vocabulary. `Contact.reviewed` is the worst of them: it puts a per-user workflow state onto a shared record, so when two Full-timers walk with the same trainee it is ambiguous who reviewed it. ## What Macro does Separates two orthogonal axes and applies both uniformly to any entity: **read** (I have seen it) and **done** (I have dealt with it). `inboxReads` today only models "scanned", which is passive — there is no way to clear something off your list. ## Scope - One per-user store keyed by entity ref (`contact:<id>`, `interaction:<id>`, `thread:<id>` — the shape `inboxReads.ts` already uses), with `read` and `done` as separate axes. - Migrate `inboxReads`, `convHides`, `messageHides` behind it. - Leave `Notification.readBy` alone for now — it is genuinely shared state, not a per-device preference. - Plan the `Contact.reviewed` migration but do not remove the field in this issue. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Existing inbox-read and hide behaviour is unchanged from the user's point of view - [ ] A `done` axis exists and is independently settable from `read` - [ ] Unit tests cover set/clear/subscribe on both axes and the migration from each legacy store

title: [Macro study] Adopt product patterns from the Macro codebase (tracking)
body: Tracking issue for work adopting product patterns from a read-only study of [macro-inc/macro](https://github.com/macro-inc/macro) (AGPLv3, SolidJS + Rust all-in-one workspace). ## Why Macro's CRM, tasks, docs, and channels map closely onto People/The Journey, to-dos, Coordination Notes, and Messages. Their product decisions are stances rather than infrastructure, so they port even though none of their code does. Their core arguments: - **Trackers go stale** because logging costs a context switch — so make creating an entry possible from wherever the decision is actually made. - **Records should build themselves**; only judgment (stage) is manual. - **You should check one thing** to know what needs your attention, and "done" must be a real verb distinct from "seen." - **A record's notes ARE the chat system** — a separate comments box always loses to where the conversation really happens. ## Scaled down deliberately Macro serves ~15 engineers living in the tool 8 hours a day. This app serves four roles who open it a few times a week, often on a phone. Keyboard-first navigation (vim keys, `c`/`g` leader grammar) was evaluated and **declined**; splits/window management, the filter AST, the properties system, and AI Signal/Noise sorting were also declined as poor fits. ## Scope multiplier Every design-touching item lands in up to three places: the desktop view, its `*Mobile.tsx` twin (7 such pairs exist), and the React Native app in `apps/mobile/`. This is the main reason the code-only foundation goes first — it is written once and shared. ## Phase 1 — foundation, code only, unblocked Nothing here needs design input; all four can proceed in parallel. - [ ] #326 — Unify read/done state into one per-user model **(prerequisite for the merged feed)** - [ ] #327 — Shared date bucketing util **(feeds the merged feed's grouping)** - [ ] #328 — Frecency ranking in Global Search - [ ] #329 — Audit and derive Contact activity fields ## Phase 2 — design assets Merged attention feed · shared row action menu · contact pill + hover preview · merged thread tab · role-aware first-run checklist · four "Make a to-do" affordances. ## Phase 3 — build against the designs - [ ] #330 — Merge attention surfaces into one feed with a done action - [ ] #331 — Notification stacking by target - [ ] #332 — Shared action vocabulary + shared row menu - [ ] #333 — One conversation thread per person; retire the admin Comments tab ⚠️ **has a privacy decision to make first** - [ ] #334 — Live contact pill with hover preview - [ ] #335 — Role-aware first-run checklist - [ ] #336 — Four to-do creation entry points - [ ] #337 — Expand the ⌘K palette + central shortcut registry ## Testing Per `CLAUDE.md` §6 all of this is logic/data/permissions code, so TDD is mandatory — failing test first. Coverage thresholds in `vitest.config.ts` ratchet up only.

title: Auto-create a GitHub issue when feedback is submitted
body: ## Context / Problem Feedback submitted through the in-app feedback module (the "Leave a note" FAB and the `/feedback` page) lands only in the Firestore `feedback` collection and the admin Feedback list (`/admin/feedback`). There is no bridge into our engineering workflow, so actionable feedback has to be manually re-entered as GitHub issues. We want submissions to automatically open a GitHub issue in this repo so they show up in normal triage. ## Proposed behavior When a user submits feedback, automatically open a GitHub issue in `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`: - **Trigger on all four kinds** — thought, idea, "something's off", request. - Map kind → labels: `off` → `bug`; `thought`/`idea`/`request` → `enhancement`; plus a new `feedback` label (needs creating). - Title: short summary from the kind + first line of the message. - Body: full message, submitter name/email, kind, and a link to the admin feedback entry. - **Link back:** store the created issue's number/URL on the feedback doc and show a "View on GitHub" link in the admin Feedback list (`/admin/feedback`). - **Best-effort:** a GitHub failure must NOT block or revert the in-app success state (mirror the existing `logActivity` / `sendNotification` pattern). ## Suggested implementation - Feedback is written client-side directly to Firestore today (`addDoc(collection(db, 'feedback'), …)`) in `src/components/FeedbackFAB.tsx` and `src/views/SubmitFeedback.tsx`. Keep that write; add a best-effort backend call afterward. - Add an endpoint (e.g. `POST /api/feedback/github-issue`) in `server.ts` (Express on Cloud Run, fronted by the Cloudflare proxy in `functions/api/[[path]].ts`) that creates the issue via the GitHub REST API and writes the issue URL/number back onto the feedback doc with the Admin SDK. - Store a `GITHUB_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT with Issues:write on this repo, or a GitHub App token) as a Cloud Run env var — never exposed to the client. - Create a `feedback` label in the repo. - Add optional `githubIssueUrl` / `githubIssueNumber` to the `Feedback` type (`src/types.ts`) and render the link in `src/views/FeedbackList.tsx`. ## Acceptance criteria - Submitting any feedback kind opens a GitHub issue with appropriate labels. - The issue references the submitter + message; the feedback doc / admin list links to the issue. - A GitHub outage does not break feedback submission. --- _Filed as a tracking issue; implementation not started yet._

title: Epic: Raise unit-test coverage to 90%
body: **Goal:** raise unit-test coverage from the current ~24% baseline to **90%**, enforced in CI. Today `vitest.config.ts` enforces only **22% lines / 15% branches / 15% functions / 22% statements**. Most of the app's logic lives in large, untested React view/modal components. This epic tracks a deliberate, phased climb to 90%. ### Strategy A single PR jumping to 90% isn't reviewable. Each child below is **one PR** that adds tests for a layer and **ratchets the `thresholds` in `vitest.config.ts` up to just under the new measured number** — so coverage can never regress, and CI (`npm run test:coverage`) enforces each step. We build outward from cheap, high-signal pure logic to the expensive UI components. Indicative targets are guides; the implementer reads the actual `coverage/coverage-summary.json` after each PR and sets the new threshold a few points below it. ### Pragmatic exclusions (so 90% is real, not padded) Added to `coverage.exclude` in P0: - `src/main.tsx` (bootstrap) - `src/lib/yjsRtdbProvider.ts` (Yjs⇄RTDB CRDT transport — needs an emulator/integration harness, out of scope for unit coverage) - `src/vite-env.d.ts` - `src/constants.ts` (placeholder data) - the `VITE_E2E_MODE` `window.__e2eSignIn` block in `src/lib/firebase.ts` ### Phases - [ ] **P0** — stabilize the coverage harness (prerequisite; no threshold bump) → #56 - [ ] **P1** — unit-test `src/lib` pure logic (≈ +8–12pts) → #57 - [ ] **P2** — providers & shared UI primitives (≈ +6–8pts) → #58 - [ ] **P3** — core views (≈ +12–16pts) → #59 - [ ] **P4** — large views (≈ +14–18pts) → #60 - [ ] **P5** — modals & layout (≈ +10–14pts) → #61 - [ ] **P6** — enforce 90% thresholds in CI (final ratchet) → #62 ### Definition of done - `vitest.config.ts` thresholds at the 90% target (lines/statements 90; branches/functions trail as conventional). - `npm run test:coverage` green; CI enforces it on every PR. - Every phase issue closed.

title: Move Firestore-rules deploy to keyless auth (Workload Identity Federation)
body: ## Goal Replace the long-lived service-account **key** used by the Firestore-rules deploy with **keyless auth via Workload Identity Federation (WIF)** — GitHub's OIDC token is exchanged for short-lived GCP credentials, so there's no JSON key stored in a GitHub secret. > Terminology: for CI/workloads this is **Workload Identity Federation** (a *Workload* Identity Pool + OIDC provider). "Workforce pools" are the sibling feature for human users from an external IdP — not what we want here. ## Why Follow-up to #44 / #46. Today [`.github/workflows/deploy-firestore-rules.yml`](.github/workflows/deploy-firestore-rules.yml) (lines 76–79) authenticates with: ```yaml - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2 with: credentials_json: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }} ``` That secret holds a **long-lived private key** for `github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Downsides: - A non-expiring credential sits in GitHub secrets; if it leaks, it's valid until manually revoked. - No rotation story — keys silently age forever (`validBeforeTime: 9999`). - During #46 we hit exactly the failure mode this invites: the secret was holding the *wrong* SA's key and nobody could tell (secrets are write-only). WIF removes the key entirely. With WIF: tokens are minted per-run, expire in minutes, and access is scoped by an attribute condition to **this repo only**. ## Current state (already in place) - Deploy SA `github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com` exists and holds the 3 roles a rules deploy needs: `roles/firebaserules.admin`, `roles/datastore.indexAdmin`, `roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer`. - Project: `sac-campus-hub` (project number `914549253362`). - Repo: `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`. ## Setup (one-time, GCP side) ```bash PROJECT_ID=sac-campus-hub PROJECT_NUMBER=914549253362 POOL=github-actions PROVIDER=github REPO=Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker SA=github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com # 1. Workload Identity Pool gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create "$POOL" \ --project="$PROJECT_ID" --location=global --display-name="GitHub Actions" # 2. OIDC provider, locked to this repo (the attribute-condition is required) gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers create-oidc "$PROVIDER" \ --project="$PROJECT_ID" --location=global --workload-identity-pool="$POOL" \ --display-name="GitHub" \ --issuer-uri="https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \ --attribute-mapping="google.subject=assertion.sub,attribute.repository=assertion.repository" \ --attribute-condition="assertion.repository == '${REPO}'" # 3. Let this repo's tokens impersonate the deploy SA gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding "$SA" \ --project="$PROJECT_ID" \ --role="roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser" \ --member="principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/projects/${PROJECT_NUMBER}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${POOL}/attribute.repository/${REPO}" ``` Provider resource name for the workflow: `projects/914549253362/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions/providers/github` ## Workflow change ```yaml permissions: contents: read id-token: write # required for OIDC # ...in the deploy job, replace the auth step: - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2 with: project_id: sac-campus-hub workload_identity_provider: projects/914549253362/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-actions/providers/github service_account: github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com ``` The action still exports `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (now a short-lived token file), so the `firebase deploy` step needs no change. Update the file's header comment (lines 6–9) which currently describes the key-based flow. ## Cutover & cleanup (after a green WIF run) - [ ] Confirm `workflow_dispatch` + a real push both deploy green via WIF. - [ ] Delete the GitHub secret `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`. - [ ] Delete `github-action@`'s user-managed key `63fafb9d4edaa333c8060133ed5814a41419b9e9` (`gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete …`) so no long-lived key remains. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] WIF pool + OIDC provider created, scoped to `Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker`. - [ ] `github-action@` granted `roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` for the repo's principalSet. - [ ] Workflow uses `workload_identity_provider` + `service_account`, with `id-token: write`. - [ ] Deploy is green with **no** `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` secret present. - [ ] Old key and secret removed. _Refs: #44 (auto-deploy), #46 (credential validation + the wrong-key incident)._

title: Confirm Firestore rules auto-deploy works after #44 merges
body: Follow-up to #44, which adds automated Firestore **rules** deployment on merge to `main`. ## Why this issue exists The deploy credential (`FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` secret) can't be fully validated before merge: GitHub secrets are write-only, and `workflow_dispatch` only works once the workflow is on the default branch. So the first real, end-to-end test is the auto-run that fires **when #44 merges**. ## Validated pre-merge ✅ - Secret `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` exists on the repo (set 2026-06-15). - Service account `github-action@sac-campus-hub.iam.gserviceaccount.com` exists and is enabled. - It holds the exact roles `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules` needs: - `roles/firebaserules.admin` — writes the ruleset/release. - `roles/datastore.indexAdmin` — satisfies the CLI's pre-flight permission check for the `firestore` target (`datastore.indexes.*`), required even for rules-only deploys. - Workflow wiring (`credentials_json: ${{ secrets.FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}`) is correct. ## To confirm after merge ⏳ - [ ] Merge #44 → the **Deploy Firestore Rules** workflow auto-runs (push to `main` hits the path filter). - [ ] `test-rules` job (Firestore emulator) passes. - [ ] `deploy` job authenticates via `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` (no auth error). - [ ] Rules publish to the **named** database `ai-studio-43298cca-4d70-4c5d-bada-c10ab66ab897` (not `(default)`) — confirm in Firebase Console → Firestore → Rules, or via the deploy log. - [ ] Verify the pending `board_sessions` / `board_notes` rules from #42 are now live. - [ ] Close this issue once the first run is green. ## If the deploy job fails on auth Most likely the pasted secret JSON is malformed/truncated. Re-paste the full service-account key JSON into the `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` secret and re-run the failed job.

title: Inconsistent error state across data views (stuck skeletons / silent failures on Firestore errors)
body: ## Background `handleFirestoreError` (`src/lib/firebase.ts:68`) **throws** after logging. PR #43 fixed the cases where a `setLoading(false)` sat *after* the throw (dead code → skeleton stuck forever). But that PR deliberately left a broader gap: **there is no consistent error state across the data views.** Today data views (Attendance, Dashboard, MyDay, Directory, OutreachBoard, History, PrayerList) only track `loading`. On a list error there are two bad outcomes: 1. **Stuck skeleton** — if the listener that owns `setLoading(false)` is the one that errors, loading never clears. 2. **Silent empty/partial list** — if a *different* listener errors after loading was already cleared, the user just sees missing/empty data with no indication anything failed. Users can't distinguish "no data yet" / "empty" / "load failed", and there's no reusable error UI (only `Settings`/`SignUp` have local form-level `error` state). ## Affected listeners (error callbacks that never clear/​surface state) Multi-listener views where `setLoading(false)` is only in the *first* success callback, so other listeners' errors are invisible and the owning listener's error hangs the skeleton: - `src/views/Dashboard.tsx` — loading cleared only at `:83` (contacts success); error callbacks at `:85` `:91` `:97` `:103` `:133` `:142` - `src/views/MyDay.tsx` — loading cleared only at `:113`; error callbacks at `:115` `:121` `:127` `:133` `:161` `:170` `:189` - `src/views/History.tsx` — loading cleared only at `:252` (activities success); error callbacks at `:230` (contacts) `:254` (activities) Secondary listeners with no error surface (loading driven by a sibling listener): - `src/views/Directory.tsx` — contacts `:152`, interactions `:202`, comments `:211` - `src/views/OutreachBoard.tsx` — contacts `:305`, interactions `:342`, comments `:351` - `src/views/Attendance.tsx` — contacts `:98` ## Options considered (pick one when scheduled) 1. **Shared error UI + retry (recommended)** — add an `error` state per data view, set it in each error callback (before the throw), and render one reusable component, e.g. `Couldn't load {label} — Reload`. Distinguishes failure from empty; recoverable. (`onSnapshot` auto-retries on reconnect, but permission-denied won't recover — a `location.reload()` action is the practical retry.) 2. **Shared error message, no retry** — same component, display-only. 3. **Just clear loading everywhere** — generalize PR #43 so every error callback clears loading before the throw. No more stuck skeletons, but failures still look like empty lists (no explicit error message). ## Notes - Keep the established ordering invariant: **clear state before calling `handleFirestoreError`**, since it throws (see PR #43 and `CoordinationNotes.tsx` as the reference). - Whatever the choice, apply it uniformly to all the views/listeners listed above for consistency.

title: The Journey board: header count mismatch + 'Add to {stage}' doesn't prefill stage
body: Two cosmetic/UX follow-ups found while reviewing the Outreach Board reskin ([PR #28](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker/pull/28), Overhaul #12). Neither is a crash or data issue — splitting them out so #28 can land. ## 1. Header total doesn't reconcile with the per-stage breakdown In [`src/views/OutreachBoard.tsx`](https://github.com/Shir0o/cisa-campus-work-traker/blob/main/src/views/OutreachBoard.tsx) the prose header bolds `filteredContacts.length` (which **includes** unmapped/unassigned contacts) but the per-stage breakdown sums only `getStageContactsArr(s.label).length` for **active** stages. **Effect:** when any contact has a stage not in the active stages list (shown in the separate "Unassigned" column), the numbers don't add up — e.g. *"10 people walking it — 2 first contact, 3 second contact, 3 regular"* (sums to 8, not 10). Looks like a bug to the user. **Fix options:** base the bold count on the per-stage sum, or append an "N unassigned" term when `unmappedContacts.length > 0`. ## 2. "Add to {stage}" / "Welcome someone new" footer buttons don't prefill the stage The column footer buttons call `openNewContact()`, which opens the new-contact modal with **no stage argument** (`useLayout().openNewContact: () => setIsNewContactModalOpen(true)` in `src/App.tsx`). **Effect:** clicking *"Add to Regular"* and saving lands the contact in the modal's default stage, not Regular — the label overpromises. The "Unassigned" column's *"Add to Unassigned"* is likewise misleading. **Fix options:** thread an optional `initialStage` through `openNewContact` / `NewContactModal` and prefill it, or soften the labels (e.g. a single "Welcome someone new" everywhere) until prefill is wired. --- _Found during local code review of #28; the PR-Reviewer bot rated #12 fully compliant. Out of scope for #28 (reskin-only)._

title: Epic: Design overhaul — "Field notes" warm/pastoral reskin
body: ## What this is A full reskin of the CISA Campus Work Tracker from its current **Material Design 3 / purple** look into **"Field notes"** — a warm, editorial, pastoral design. Mocked up in [Claude Design](https://claude.ai/design) and exported as a handoff bundle. **Design reference** (PR #7): `docs/design/` — start with `docs/design/project/CLAUDE.md` (master per-screen spec) and `docs/design/project/styles.css` (design system). ## The brief The original felt "too dense and technical" — a dev-tool / sales-CRM skin (near-black bg, monospace ID codes like `C-0142`, KPI sparklines, "Stage Board" pipeline framing) on top of genuinely human, pastoral data. Goal: **keep all features, reskin to feel warm and people-first.** Design language: - **Type:** Newsreader serif for headings/greetings, Hanken Grotesk sans for body. No visible monospace. - **Palette:** slate-blue accent on cool paper; sage success; stage tones accent/amber/teal/violet (slate-blue / terracotta / sage / plum) at matched chroma. - **Tone:** metrics demoted to quiet footers ("Numbers are just a way of noticing people."), DB IDs hidden, nav relabeled to human language, kanban reframed as a warm "journey" not a sales pipeline. - Light ("warm paper") is the **default**; dark matters too. Both devices matter. ## Locked decisions - **Keep** the permissions/RBAC UI (enforcement + Settings "Roles & access") — reskin only. - **Include** all four net-new features: Global Search (⌘K), Notifications bell, Feedback FAB reskin, "My Day" cockpit. - **Google Sheets sync:** reskin in place; flag for a later keep/remove decision. - **One screen at a time.** ## Work (sequenced — #9 and #10 block the rest) - [x] #9 — Foundation: Field Notes tokens, fonts & global styles - [x] #10 — Shell: sidebar + topbar + nav relabel - [x] #11 — Today (Dashboard) - [x] #12 — The Journey (Outreach Board) - [x] #13 — People (Directory + contact profile) - [x] #14 — Gatherings (Attendance) - [x] #15 — Prayer - [x] #16 — Looking back (History) - [x] #17 — Settings reskin (keep RBAC) - [x] #18 — "My Day" — Full-timer cockpit (new screen) - [x] #19 — Global Search (⌘K) - [x] #20 — Notifications — "What's stirring" - [x] #21 — Feedback FAB reskin - [x] #22 — Sign-up reskin - [x] #24 — The Board — Coordination Notes (warm re-derive)

title: Automate E2E tests for role-based permission matrix (4 roles, real login)
body: ## Goal Add automated **end-to-end tests for the role-based permission matrix** (PR #3) so the four role paths are checked on every PR instead of by hand. Each role signs in as a **real Firebase email/password test user** and we assert landing route, sidebar nav filtering, and route-guard redirects. This was verified manually in a real browser for all four roles (localhost + the Cloudflare preview); this issue captures how to automate it. ## Current state Scaffolding already landed in PR #3 and can be reused: - `playwright.config.ts` - `e2e/permissions.spec.ts` - `e2e/helpers/auth.ts` - `e2e/.test-credentials.example.json` (template; real file is gitignored) - `e2e/README.md` - `scripts/seed-test-user-docs.ts` (firebase-admin seeder) The app now also has an **email/password sign-in form** (added in `a038cc6`), so tests can drive the real login UI — no test-only auth hook required. ## Roles under test | Display name | Internal role | Test login env | | ------------ | ------------- | -------------- | | Full-timer | `admin` | `fulltimer` | | Trainee | `manager` | `trainee` | | Student | `operator` | `student` | | Community | `viewer` | `community` | Expected matrix (source of truth: `src/lib/permissions.ts`): | Route | min role | viewer | operator | manager | admin | |-------|----------|:------:|:--------:|:-------:|:-----:| | `/` dashboard | operator | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | `/directory` | operator | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | `/board` stage | manager | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | | `/history` | manager | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | | `/admin/feedback` | admin | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | | `/attendance` `/prayer` `/settings` | viewer | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Viewer default route is `/attendance`; everyone else defaults to `/`. --- ## Prerequisites (one-time) ### 1. Test users exist in Firebase Auth (email/password) and have **approved `/users/{uid}` docs** The app signs out any authenticated user without an approved user doc, so this is required. Two ways: - **In-app invite (no service account):** sign in as an admin → Settings → Add Member → invite the four emails with roles Full-timer/Trainee/Student/Community. The approved `/users` doc is auto-created on each user's first sign-in. - **Seed script (service account / ADC):** ```bash GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/sa.json npm run seed:e2e-users ``` ### 2. Credentials file (gitignored) ```bash cp e2e/.test-credentials.example.json e2e/.test-credentials.json # fill in the real emails + passwords ``` Shape: ```json { "fulltimer": { "email": "<email>", "password": "<pw>", "role": "admin", "label": "Full-timer" }, "trainee": { "email": "<email>", "password": "<pw>", "role": "manager", "label": "Trainee" }, "student": { "email": "<email>", "password": "<pw>", "role": "operator", "label": "Student" }, "community": { "email": "<email>", "password": "<pw>", "role": "viewer", "label": "Community" } } ``` ### 3. `VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY` available to the dev server / build `firebase-applet-config.json` ships with a blank `apiKey`; the dev server reads `VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY` from `.env`. CI must provide it as a secret. --- ## Implementation plan ### `playwright.config.ts` ```ts import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test'; // Run against a deployed preview by setting E2E_BASE_URL; otherwise boot the dev server. const baseURL = process.env.E2E_BASE_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000'; export default defineConfig({ testDir: './e2e', fullyParallel: true, workers: process.env.CI ? 2 : undefined, // Firebase Auth occasionally needs a retry on a cold page load; keep this small. retries: process.env.CI ? 2 : 1, reporter: process.env.CI ? [['github'], ['html', { open: 'never' }]] : 'list', use: { baseURL, trace: 'on-first-retry', // Tall enough that the sidebar footer (logout) is on-screen for 7-item roles (see #4). viewport: { width: 1280, height: 1000 }, }, projects: [{ name: 'chromium', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] } }], webServer: process.env.E2E_BASE_URL ? undefined : { command: 'npm run dev', port: 3000, reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI, timeout: 60_000 }, }); ``` ### `e2e/helpers/auth.ts` Drive the real email/password form. **Each Playwright test runs in its own isolated browser context**, so there is no shared Firebase auth state between roles — no logout step and none of the persistence races seen during manual testing. ```ts import { type Page } from '@playwright/test'; import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'; import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'; import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path'; const dir = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)); export type Role = 'fulltimer' | 'trainee' | 'student' | 'community'; interface Cred { email: string; password: string; role: string; label: string } export function creds(): Record<Role, Cred> { try { return JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(dir, '../.test-credentials.json'), 'utf8')); } catch { throw new Error('Missing e2e/.test-credentials.json — copy from .test-credentials.example.json'); } } export async function signInAs(page: Page, role: Role) { const { email, password } = creds()[role]; await page.goto('/'); await page.getByPlaceholder('Email').waitFor({ state: 'visible' }); // Let Firebase Auth finish initialising before submitting (prevents a cold-load race). await page.waitForTimeout(1500); await page.getByPlaceholder('Email').fill(email); await page.getByPlaceholder('Password').fill(password); await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in with email/i }).click(); // The app shell (sidebar) only renders once authenticated AND approved. await page.getByLabel('Main Navigation').waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20_000 }); } ``` ### `e2e/permissions.spec.ts` ```ts import { test, expect, type Page } from '@playwright/test'; import { signInAs, type Role } from './helpers/auth'; const MATRIX: Record<Role, { landing: RegExp; navPresent: string[]; navAbsent: string[]; allowed: string[]; denied: { from: string; to: RegExp }[]; }> = { community: { landing: /\/attendance$/, navPresent: ['Attendance', 'Prayer List', 'Settings'], navAbsent: ['Dashboard', 'Stage', 'Contacts', 'History'], allowed: ['/attendance', '/prayer', '/settings'], denied: [ { from: '/', to: /\/attendance$/ }, { from: '/board', to: /\/attendance$/ }, { from: '/directory', to: /\/attendance$/ }, { from: '/admin/feedback', to: /\/attendance$/ }, ], }, student: { landing: /\/$/, navPresent: ['Dashboard', 'Contacts', 'Attendance', 'Prayer List', 'Settings'], navAbsent: ['Stage', 'History'], allowed: ['/', '/directory', '/attendance', '/prayer', '/settings'], denied: [ { from: '/board', to: /\/$/ }, { from: '/history', to: /\/$/ }, { from: '/admin/feedback', to: /\/$/ }, ], }, trainee: { landing: /\/$/, navPresent: ['Dashboard', 'Stage', 'Contacts', 'History', 'Attendance', 'Prayer List', 'Settings'], navAbsent: [], allowed: ['/', '/board', '/directory', '/history', '/attendance', '/prayer', '/settings'], denied: [{ from: '/admin/feedback', to: /\/$/ }], }, fulltimer: { landing: /\/$/, navPresent: ['Dashboard', 'Stage', 'Contacts', 'History', 'Attendance', 'Prayer List', 'Settings'], navAbsent: [], allowed: ['/', '/board', '/directory', '/history', '/attendance', '/prayer', '/settings', '/admin/feedback'], denied: [], }, }; const navText = (page: Page) => page.getByLabel('Main Navigation').getByRole('link').allInnerTexts().then(t => t.join(' ')); for (const role of Object.keys(MATRIX) as Role[]) { const m = MATRIX[role]; test.describe(`role: ${role}`, () => { test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => { await signInAs(page, role); }); test('lands on the correct default route', async ({ page }) => { await expect(page).toHaveURL(m.landing); }); test('sidebar shows only permitted nav items', async ({ page }) => { const labels = await navText(page); for (const item of m.navPresent) expect(labels).toContain(item); for (const item of m.navAbsent) expect(labels).not.toContain(item); }); test('allowed routes stay put', async ({ page }) => { for (const route of m.allowed) { await page.goto(route); await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(route.replace(/\//g, '\\/') + '$')); } }); if (m.denied.length) { test('denied routes redirect to fallback', async ({ page }) => { for (const d of m.denied) { await page.goto(d.from); await expect(page).toHaveURL(d.to); } }); } }); } ``` ### `package.json` ```jsonc "scripts": { "test:e2e": "playwright test", "seed:e2e-users": "tsx scripts/seed-test-user-docs.ts" } ``` ### Run it ```bash # local dev server (auto-started by Playwright) VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY=<key> npm run test:e2e # against a deployed preview E2E_BASE_URL=https://<preview>.pages.dev npm run test:e2e ``` --- ## Why this avoids the manual-testing pitfalls - **No logout / account-switch race.** Playwright gives each test a fresh, isolated browser context, so every role gets a clean Firebase auth state. The manual run shared one browser and had to log out between roles, which caused session-persist races and hit the clipped logout button (#4). Tests don't. - **`displayName` provisioning bug is already fixed** (`a038cc6`): email/password accounts have a `null` displayName, which the Firestore rules reject on first-login `setDoc`. Without that fix, first-login provisioning fails with *"Missing or insufficient permissions"* and the app hangs on the loading skeleton. - **Cold-load race** mitigated by the short settle in `signInAs` plus 1–2 Playwright retries. - **Footer/logout viewport issue (#4)** avoided by a 1000px-tall viewport (and tests never click logout anyway). ## CI integration ```yaml # .github/workflows/e2e.yml (sketch) name: E2E permissions on: [pull_request] jobs: e2e: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: { node-version: 20, cache: npm } - run: npm ci - run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium - name: Write test credentials run: echo "$E2E_TEST_CREDENTIALS" > e2e/.test-credentials.json env: { E2E_TEST_CREDENTIALS: ${{ secrets.E2E_TEST_CREDENTIALS }} } - run: npm run test:e2e env: { VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY }} } - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 if: failure() with: { name: playwright-report, path: playwright-report/, retention-days: 7 } ``` Secrets required: - `VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY` — Firebase web API key - `E2E_TEST_CREDENTIALS` — the JSON contents of `e2e/.test-credentials.json` Notes: - These tests hit the **real** Firebase project. Keep them **read-only** (navigation/redirect assertions only — no data mutation) and consider gating on a label or running against the preview URL rather than on every push. - Make the check **non-blocking** until it's proven stable, then add it to the branch ruleset. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `npm run test:e2e` green locally against the dev server for all four roles - [ ] Same green against a deployed preview via `E2E_BASE_URL` - [ ] CI workflow runs on PRs with credentials from secrets - [ ] `.test-credentials.json` and `playwright-report/` are gitignored (already are) - [ ] README documents provisioning + how to run Related: #4 (logout/account-switching UX), PR #3 (the permission feature being tested).

title: Account switching: session sometimes fails to persist after quick re-login
body: ## Summary While verifying the role-based permissions in a real browser (signing in as each of the four role test users), I hit two problems related to **switching between user accounts**. ## 1. Log out control can be unreachable (primary, actionable) The **Log out** button lives in the sidebar footer (`src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx`, the `mt-auto` footer block). The sidebar (`h-screen`, `overflow-hidden`) and its nav-items container are both `overflow-hidden`, so on **shorter viewports** the footer can be pushed below the fold for roles that show many nav items: - **Full-timer (admin)** and **Trainee (manager)** see all **7** nav items → the footer (Log out / Collapse) is clipped and not clickable. - **Student (operator, 5)** and **Community (viewer, 3)** have fewer items → logout is reachable. **Impact:** an admin/manager on a laptop with a shorter window (or OS chrome reducing height) may be unable to log out / switch accounts from the desktop sidebar. **Repro:** sign in as an admin, shrink the window height (~660px content), observe the Log out button is not visible/clickable in the sidebar. **Suggested fix:** make the nav-items region scrollable (`overflow-y-auto`) instead of `overflow-hidden`, and/or guarantee the footer is always pinned/visible regardless of item count. ## 2. Session occasionally fails to persist right after re-login (secondary, lower confidence) When logging out and signing back in as a different user **quickly**, the new sign-in sometimes does not stick — the app returns to the welcome/sign-in screen instead of the dashboard, and a retry is needed. This was intermittent and may be a Firebase auth-persistence timing issue when a sign-in happens immediately after a sign-out/reload. Worth confirming whether real users hit it (e.g. shared kiosk / quick account switches). ## Context Found during PR #3 (role-based access control). The permission logic itself works correctly for all four roles; this issue is specifically about the **logout / account-switching UX**.
